q2_minimal_safe_expired_recovery.rationale: In uos/telegram-runtime/20261001-1150, tasks FORMAL_FIX and STORE_TRANSPORT_REVIEW both carry expired October 1 leases. Because risk-priority-check audits the complete plan and fails closed on ANY expired lease, single-task reclaim logic deadlocks. A minimal safe recovery protocol must be executed before runtime tasks can proceed.

proposed_minimal_safe_recovery.step_1_exact_closed_set: Target exclusively the exact expired task set { plan_id: 'uos/telegram-runtime/20261001-1150', tasks: ['FORMAL_FIX', 'STORE_TRANSPORT_REVIEW'] } with their original workers, attempts, and expired deadline timestamps.
proposed_minimal_safe_recovery.step_2_quiescence_proof: Execute /proc and process tree inspection to prove that no active processes for those workers exist or hold open file descriptors/locks on the store or evidence paths.
proposed_minimal_safe_recovery.step_3_atomic_coordinator_transaction: Execute a single reviewed coordinator transaction in Sa-plan that atomically releases or resets the lease for both tasks simultaneously, accompanied by a signed observation receipt.
proposed_minimal_safe_recovery.step_4_immutable_history_preservation: Original failure receipts, test logs, and expired lease evidence must NOT be modified or deleted. New receipts must link to the original evidence by SHA-256.
proposed_minimal_safe_recovery.step_5_no_blanket_waiver: Ordinary active-check and preflight fences remain fully enforced. No global flags like --skip-expired-checks or relaxed time boundaries are permitted.
proposed_minimal_safe_recovery.step_6_negative_refusal_tests: Machine-verify that attempting recovery on an incomplete set, a mismatched attempt, or an active process returns an immediate fail-closed refusal.

q3_telegram_feature_inventory.rationale: Stages T1, T4, and T5 provide a solid foundation for core bot commands, formatting, and delivery, but omitted several crucial production Telegram feature families that must be represented in the inventory and Sa-plan task breakdown.

omitted_or_under_specified_feature_famil.detail: Telegram Bot API returns HTTP 409 Conflict if two pollers query getUpdates simultaneously with the same bot token. A strict filesystem or process-level exclusive lease mutex must guarantee that legacy pollers (e.g. tools/telegram_client.ml, apps/cepaf_gleam telegram.gleam) are fully quiesced before the new supervised poller starts.

Interactive buttons produce callback_query updates requiring answerCallbackQuery within 30 seconds to dismiss client loading spinners. The ingress handler must route and acknowledge callback queries explicitly.

omitted_or_under_specified_feature_famil.feature: Telegram Mini-App WebApp initData HMAC Verification
omitted_or_under_specified_feature_famil.detail: If Mini-App routes are exposed, initData must be cryptographically validated using HMAC-SHA256 with key derived from HMAC_SHA256('WebAppData', bot_token), enforcing auth_date freshness (<24h) to prevent replay attacks.

Messages exceeding 4096 UTF-8 characters must be chunked at clean paragraph/newline boundaries rather than raw byte slices. MarkdownV2 reserved characters (_ * [ ] ( ) ~ ` > # + - = | { } . !) must be escaped systematically to avoid HTTP 400 Bad Request delivery drops.

Telegram enforces global limits of 30 messages/second and per-chat limits of 1 message/second (20/minute for groups). An in-memory token bucket rate limiter in the Gleam outbox supervisor is mandatory to prevent HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
Photos, documents, and voice notes must have strict size limits (e.g. max 20MB download cap) and hash validation before handoff; unvetted executable files must be quarantined.

state_machine_and_uncertainty_review.notes: Transition from PENDING -> SENDING -> DELIVERED only on HTTP 200 with matching chat_id and message_id is correct. Network timeouts and HTTP 5xx during send MUST transition to UNCERTAIN with administrative reconciliation; blind automatic retry is strictly barred to avoid duplicate execution.

q4_integration_ordering.rationale: The progression from T0 (tool/recovery) -> T1 (inventory) -> T2 (native store repair) -> T3 (Gleam codec/transport) -> T4 (supervised poller) -> T5 (private simulated E2E) -> T6 (release prep) -> T7 (single-recipient live acceptance) -> T8 (Codex JJ merge) strictly respects UOS isolation boundaries.
essential_isolation_barriers: Stages T0 through T6 must execute exclusively against hermetic mock/simulated Telegram Bot API endpoints; no live Telegram network traffic or production tokens.
Stage T7 requires explicit operator authorization for a single designated recipient chat_id and a bounded test message.
Stage T8 is executed solely by the Codex integration writer in standalone Jujutsu; EV ceiling remains pinned at EV-93.

residuals.name: init_ddl_and_meta_not_one_transaction
residuals.problem: Schema DDL and metadata insertion are executed across separate statements without an enclosing BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT transaction. Interruption leaves a partial or corrupt database.
residuals.required_fix: Wrap all DDL tables, indexes, triggers, and metadata insertion in a single atomic IMMEDIATE transaction, validating schema_version and pragma foreign_keys immediately after commit.

residuals.name: path_ancestors_unchecked
residuals.problem: safe_db_path verifies lstat on the leaf database file but does not check ancestor directories. An attacker or symlinked directory component could allow path traversal or unauthorized redirection.
residuals.required_fix: Walk all directory components up to the repository root / authorized storage base using lstat, ensuring every component is a regular directory owned by the current UID and not writable by others.

residuals.name: decoded_values_no_utf8_or_domain_json_parsing
residuals.problem: The native store accepts base64-decoded byte payloads without verifying valid UTF-8 encoding or syntactic structure for JSON-typed fields.
residuals.required_fix: Enforce strict UTF-8 validation and maximum payload size bounds (e.g. 1 MiB) in the native worker. Domain-specific schema validation is enforced in the Gleam layer before invoking the native worker.

residuals.name: commit_error_state_may_be_unknown
residuals.problem: When COMMIT returns SQLITE_BUSY or SQLITE_IOERR, the transaction state in SQLite is ambiguous (it may have committed to WAL or aborted). Returning a generic error causes callers to assume rollback, risking double-writes.
residuals.required_fix: Inspect sqlite3_get_autocommit(db). If autocommit is false, issue ROLLBACK; if autocommit is true or ROLLBACK fails, return explicit UNCERTAIN_COMMIT error status, directing the caller to perform idempotent lookup_operation before retry.

residuals.name: reservation_ledger_belongs_to_consumer
residuals.problem: The storage kernel attempted to maintain business-domain credit reservation accounting, violating separation of concerns and leaking domain policy into the native layer.
residuals.required_fix: Strip domain reservation accounting from the native SQLite worker. The storage kernel provides atomic Compare-And-Swap (CAS) on generation and row hash; reservation business logic belongs to the Gleam domain controller.

residuals.name: delimiter_digest_disambiguation
residuals.problem: Computing canonical request digests using simple colon/newline concatenation ('key:val') is vulnerable to ambiguity if keys or values contain delimiters.
residuals.required_fix: Use unambiguous length-prefixed encoding (e.g. '%d:%s') or RFC 8785 canonical JSON serialization for all fields contributing to the SHA-256 request digest.
